title: Lesson 43 nonpreposed and idiomatic adjectival modification technical proof

groups.title: Nonpreposed modifiers and distant supplements
groups.proposal: Use the canonical modification owner for postposed clausal modifiers while preserving their supplementary participants and possible distance from the modified head.
groups.readingJob: Show the principal head, postposed modifier, supplementary participants, and translation-versus-structure boundary.
groups.decisionSplit: Order and adjunctor marking remain the only genuine structural choices; supplement roles come from the exact clauses.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer a relative pronoun or collapse a clausal modifier into an adjective word.

groups.title: Cooperating and discontinuous modifiers
groups.proposal: Preserve cooperating preposed and nonpreposed modifiers and discontinuous head-modifier orders as typed selections in the same owner.
groups.readingJob: Show each modifier boundary, its reference contact, and any intervening clause without flattening the composition.
groups.decisionSplit: Cooperation or discontinuity is selectable only when the supplied exact Results satisfy that topology.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not derive discontinuity from token distance or surface punctuation.

groups.title: Interrogative heads and modification structure
groups.proposal: Treat interrogative pronominal NNCs as ordinary typed heads or clauses inside modification and retain supplementation-versus-modification ambiguity where both structures are licensed.
groups.readingJob: Show why English relative wording is a translation effect and identify the Nahuatl head and adjoined unit.
groups.decisionSplit: Expose a relation choice only when both exact supplementation and modification analyses are available.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a Nahuatl relative-pronoun category from English translation.

groups.title: Āc, tlêh, and other interrogative-head readings
groups.proposal: Retain the canonical owner records for āc, tlêh, and other interrogative heads while routing productive structure through the same modification relation.
groups.readingJob: Show the licensed interrogative head, in-pattern scope, structural reading, and traditional spelling analysis independently.
groups.decisionSplit: Only a genuinely ambiguous structural relation is selectable; lexical reading and spelling facts remain read-only.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not let solid writing or an English gloss authorize a grammatical parse.

groups.title: Oc cē as a modified head
groups.proposal: Preserve oc cē as an owner-recognized modified-head construction without converting its idiomatic value into a new Source class.
groups.readingJob: Show the additional-member meaning, head structure, and limits of English another.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not authorize the construction from the English gloss another.

groups.title: Cēm- singling one member from a group
groups.proposal: Use typed cēm- head identity and an exact plural group clause to license the narrow one-of-group agreement exception.
groups.readingJob: Show the singled individual, containing group, and each clause's own person-number realization.
groups.decisionSplit: Agreement patterns are derived from the supplied clauses; they are not a free exception switch.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not generalize mismatched agreement beyond the cēm- singling structure.

groups.title: Acah and ayāc one-of or none-of structures
groups.proposal: License acah and ayāc partitive modification only from their typed pronominal head identity plus the exact plural group clause.
groups.readingJob: Show candidate polarity, containing group, and the independent agreement of every clause.
groups.decisionSplit: Polarity and participant facts come from the canonical Sources, not from a broad one-none selector.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not use acah or ayāc as a general agreement-bypass token.

groups.title: Male-bonding and named-partner modification
groups.proposal: Require an owner-issued discourse Source context for male-group membership or a known named partner before licensing the corresponding narrow agreement profile.
groups.readingJob: Show speaker membership or known-participant context separately from the grammatical Result.
groups.decisionSplit: Discourse facts are typed Source information, never a lesson or example switch.
groups.controlPolicy: Reject copied context shapes and unrelated agreement mismatches.
